answers: Card orders can be tracked in the app under Cards. If tracking shows the card as sent and it has not arrived, an agent can start a trace with the delivery provider.
A replacement card is ordered the same way as a new one. If you never received it, the next step is a delivery trace, which an agent has to open for you.
clarifying_question: Was this a new card or a replacement, and did the app show it as sent?

answers: Delivery timing depends on your country and the card type; the app shows the current estimate for your order.
I cannot give a firm delivery date here. Your order status in the app is the authoritative estimate, and an agent can check it with the courier.
clarifying_question: Which card are you waiting for, and what does the app show as its status?

answers: Check that the card is activated and not frozen in the app. If it still fails, note the time, amount and merchant so an agent can check the decline.
If a payment was declined, the app usually shows a reason code. If no reason appears, a support agent needs to look at the attempt.
clarifying_question: Was the card declined, or did it stop working everywhere?

answers: Virtual cards can fail if they are not activated or if merchant or country restrictions apply. The app lists which restrictions are set on your card.
Try once more after refreshing the card details in the app. If the merchant still refuses it, an agent can check whether the merchant is blocked.
clarifying_question: Which merchant or website was the virtual card declined at?

answers: Freeze the card in the app first, then order a replacement. I am handing this to an agent so recent activity can be reviewed with you.
This needs a person: I cannot freeze a card or open a dispute. Use the app freeze control now and an agent will take over.
clarifying_question: Have you already frozen the card in the app?

answers: Freeze the card now if you still have app access. An agent will review the unrecognised transactions with you before anything is disputed.
I cannot dispute charges or promise a refund. Freeze the card in the app and I will route this to the fraud team.
clarifying_question: Which transactions do you not recognise, and have you frozen the card?

answers: Renewal is handled automatically for most cards; the app shows the expected delivery for the replacement.
If your card is close to expiry, check the renewal address in your profile. A replacement is sent to the address on file.
clarifying_question: Is the expiry date on the card itself, or shown differently in the app?

answers: PIN changes are done in the app under Card security, or at an ATM that supports PIN change. I cannot change a PIN for you.
You can set a new PIN in the app. If the option is not available, your card may need to be activated first.
clarifying_question: Do you still remember the current PIN, or has it been blocked?

answers: A blocked PIN is usually unblocked with the PIN letter or through the app. If neither works, an agent has to reset it.
Unblocking needs identity verification. I am passing this to an agent who can walk you through it.
clarifying_question: Was the PIN entered incorrectly a few times, or did it block on its own?

answers: Declines are usually limits, insufficient funds, or a merchant or country restriction. The app shows the reason for the last attempt.
If the app shows no reason, an agent needs the merchant, amount and time to check the decline.
clarifying_question: Was it an online payment or a card-present purchase?

answers: Check the merchant name in the app, as some appear under a parent company. If it still looks unfamiliar, this needs a human review.
I cannot reverse a charge. Note the date and amount, and an agent will compare it against your transaction history.
clarifying_question: What date and amount is the charge, and does the app show a merchant name?

answers: Duplicated authorisations often drop off on their own, but a settled double charge needs review by an agent.
I cannot refund a duplicate. An agent will check whether both entries settled or one is still pending.
clarifying_question: Are both charges settled, or is one still pending?

answers: Top-up limits depend on your account and verification level; the app shows the limit currently applied to you.
I cannot raise a limit. If you need a higher one, an agent can check whether your account is eligible.
clarifying_question: Which top-up method are you using, and what limit does the app show?

answers: Failed top-ups are usually a declined funding source or a limit. The app shows the status of the last attempt.
If the money left your bank but the balance did not change, an agent needs to trace it rather than retry.
clarifying_question: Did the amount leave your bank account, or did the top-up fail before charging?

answers: Pending top-ups complete after the funding source settles; the app shows the expected completion.
If it stays pending past the stated window, an agent can check the funding reference.
clarifying_question: How did you top up: another card, a bank transfer, or cash?

answers: A reverted top-up means the funding did not complete and the amount was returned. The app shows where it was sent back.
If the money has not reappeared in your funding account, an agent can trace the return.
clarifying_question: Which account was the top-up funded from?

answers: Automatic top-ups trigger when your balance drops below a level you set; the app shows the rule and its last trigger.
I cannot change the rule for you. It can be edited in the app, or an agent can explain why it did not trigger.
clarifying_question: Did the automatic top-up fail to run, or run at the wrong time?

answers: A fee for topping up by card depends on your card and account type; the app shows the fee before you confirm.
I cannot waive or refund a fee. An agent can explain which fee applied to a specific top-up.
clarifying_question: Which top-up are you looking at, and what fee does the app show?

answers: Transfer timing depends on the route and the receiving bank; the app shows an estimated arrival for each transfer.
I cannot speed up a transfer. If the estimate has passed, an agent can trace it.
clarifying_question: Was this a transfer to another bank, or within the same provider?

answers: Pending means the transfer is queued or awaiting the receiving bank. The app shows the current status and estimate.
If it stays pending beyond the estimate, an agent can request a trace.
clarifying_question: When did you send it, and what status does the app show?

answers: A failed transfer is normally returned to your balance. The app shows the failure reason and the return.
If the money has not come back, an agent needs the transfer reference to trace it.
clarifying_question: Does the app show a failure reason, and has the amount returned to your balance?

answers: A transfer can only be cancelled while it is still pending; once it reaches the receiving bank it cannot be recalled here.
I cannot cancel it. Check the status in the app first, then an agent can confirm whether a recall is possible.
clarifying_question: What status does the transfer show right now?

answers: First confirm the account details with the recipient, since wrong details send the money elsewhere. A trace needs an agent.
I cannot recall or redirect a sent transfer. An agent will need the reference and recipient details to open a trace.
clarifying_question: Have you confirmed the account details with the recipient?

answers: Fees depend on the transfer route and currency; the app shows the fee applied to each transfer.
I cannot refund a transfer fee. An agent can explain which fee applied and why.
clarifying_question: Which transfer is the fee on?

answers: Incoming transfers appear once the sending bank settles them; the app shows pending incoming amounts too.
If the sender confirms it was sent and nothing shows here, an agent can request details from the sending side.
clarifying_question: Do you know when, and from which bank, it was sent?

answers: To receive money into your account, share the account details shown in the app rather than a card number.
Incoming transfers are matched by account details, so check that the sender used exactly what the app shows.
clarifying_question: Is the sender using your account details or a card number?

answers: Bank transfers usually update after the sending bank settles. If your bank shows it as sent, the app may need a moment or a trace.
If it has been sent and your balance has not moved, an agent can check the incoming reference.
clarifying_question: Does your sending bank show the transfer as completed?

answers: Cash access depends on the card and the ATM network; the app lists which networks your card works with.
If an ATM refused the card, the network or the machine may be the cause. An agent can check restrictions on your card.
clarifying_question: Was the card refused, or did the ATM keep it?

answers: Withdrawal fees depend on the ATM operator and your account type; the app shows fees charged on each withdrawal.
I cannot refund an ATM fee. An agent can tell you which fee applied to a specific withdrawal.
clarifying_question: Which withdrawal is the fee for?

answers: Check the location and date in the app; ATM withdrawals are sometimes labelled with the operator rather than the bank.
I cannot reverse a withdrawal. An agent will review it with you and check whether the machine had a known issue.
clarifying_question: Do you remember using that ATM, and what date was it?

answers: I can check the ECB reference rate for a pair. Tell me the two currencies and any amount.
Reference rates update on business days, so I will give you the rate with the date it applies to.
clarifying_question: Which two currencies, and how much would you like converted?

answers: A currency-conversion charge depends on your card and the transaction currency; the app shows it on the statement line.
I cannot refund or waive a conversion charge. An agent can explain which rate and markup applied.
clarifying_question: Which transaction is the charge on?

answers: Currency exchange in the app is under the balance or card screen; I cannot perform the exchange for you.
If the exchange option is not shown for your currency, it may not be supported for your account type.
clarifying_question: Which currencies are you exchanging between?

answers: Card payments convert at the rate applied on the settlement date, which can differ from the purchase date. An agent can confirm the rate used.
I cannot recalculate or dispute a conversion here. An agent will compare the applied rate with the reference rate for that date.
clarifying_question: What date was the purchase, and which currency was it in?

answers: ATM withdrawals can be converted by the machine operator instead of by us, and that rate can differ. An agent can check which conversion was applied.
This needs a review of the withdrawal record rather than a live quote. I am passing it to an agent.
clarifying_question: Did the ATM offer to convert the amount for you at the time?

answers: The currencies you can hold or exchange depend on your account and region; the app lists what is available to you.
I cannot enable a currency. If one is missing from the app, an agent can confirm whether it is supported for your account.
clarifying_question: Which currency are you trying to use?

answers: Card networks and supported currencies depend on your account type and region; the app lists them for your card.
Tell me the merchant country and currency and I can say whether it is a supported combination, or pass it to an agent.
clarifying_question: Which country and currency is the merchant in?

answers: Verification usually needs a document photo and a selfie in the app; I cannot verify an identity here.
If verification failed, the app shows which step did not pass. An agent can review it once you have retried.
clarifying_question: At which step did verification stop?

answers: Identity checks are a regulatory requirement for holding an account and moving money; the app explains the specific requirement for your case.
Regulations differ by country, so the app shows the requirement that applies to you.
clarifying_question: Which country is your account registered in?

answers: Some details can be changed in the app under Profile; legal name and date of birth usually need an agent and a document.
I cannot change profile data. Tell me which field, and an agent will confirm what evidence is needed.
clarifying_question: Which detail needs changing: address, phone, name, or something else?

answers: Closing an account needs a person to confirm balances and pending transfers first. I am passing this to an agent.
Before closing, check for pending transactions, as they can fail once the account is closed.
clarifying_question: Do you have pending transfers or a remaining balance?

answers: Account availability depends on your country of residence and the documents you can provide; the app shows what is supported.
I cannot open an account for a country that is not listed. An agent can confirm the current list.
clarifying_question: Which country are you resident in?
